verdicts.evidence: An AST-based audit of the released code found 19 registered tools (≥10+), 8 stage modules, and a system prompt requiring stepwise tool execution via Claude Agent SDK streaming, but the actual end-to-end pipeline was never executed, the ReAct loop is delegated to the SDK rather than locally implemented, and the 'first' priority claim was not evaluated.

No execution was attempted: the required model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) is retired, the 306 original traces and predictions are not released, and the repository lacks an automatic success judge; paper-table concordance was explicitly not treated as reproduction evidence.

An independent JSONL parser recomputed 102 records with 102 unique IDs/queries, 18 categories, 8 stages, and tier counts {basic:40, intermediate:28, advanced:21, challenging:13}, all matching the paper's declared split; schema, duplication, and tier-complexity consistency checks passed.

The released evaluator implements the five metric families, but the official dataset lacks CRC-CODEX evaluation inputs, generated quantification outputs, and the complete ground-truth bundle needed to recompute the reported 0.953/0.902/0.368 values.

Four ground-truth files (2,013,525 rows) pass structural schema checks, but original agent predictions are absent so the reported 0.681 average similarity cannot be recomputed; the evaluator also has a row-order sensitivity bug noted as a qualification.

overall: The logbook independently verifies the SP-Bench construction (102 queries, 8 stages, 18 categories, correct tier split) and partially verifies the agent architecture through static code analysis, but none of the three numerical performance claims (SP-Bench accuracy, CRC-CODEX metrics, cell-annotation similarity) could be reproduced because original traces, predictions, and evaluation inputs are missing.
